name: Auckland Zoo Conservation Fund Small Grants Programme
summary: Small annual grants for ongoing or pilot field conservation projects in New Zealand or developing countries; applicants can be based anywhere and the grant must cover at least a quarter of the project budget.

geography.label: New Zealand or a developing country

steps: Complete and return the application form
Auckland Zoo staff review and shortlist

eligibility.rule: Project budget does not exceed NZD 40,000
Project aligns with the current round's geographic or taxonomic scope, if applicable
Not pure research: research shows applied conservation benefit or meets an identified need
The project does not fund applicant attendance at a conference, seminar, workshop or meeting
Budget excludes thesis, retrospective, prize, entertainment, social, fundraising and debt costs

status.quote: Applications have now closed. Check back later in the year for details on the next round of funding.

geography.quote: Be based in New Zealand or in a developing country (although applicants can be based anywhere in the world)

access.quote: Download, complete and return the Small Grants Programme application form.

window.quote: There is one round of the Small Grants Programme each year.

amount.quote: Small grants will be awarded up to a maximum of NZD$10,000.

effort.quote: Download, complete and return the Small Grants Programme application form.
Auckland Zoo staff will review all applications received by the submission deadline, including assessing references and other details (e.g. budgets, financial contributions from other sources).
A short-list of applications will then be forwarded for consideration to the Auckland Zoo Conservation Fund Committee, which will decide which projects will be funded

eligibility.quote: Projects must have a maximum total budget of NZD$40,000.
Projects not aligned with the geographic or taxonomic focus of the current round of grants (if applicable)
Pure research (i.e. research projects must demonstrate applied benefit to conservation and/or target an identified conservation need)
The applicant's attendance at a conference, seminar, workshop or meeting

Thesis production costs Retrospective costs Prize money Entertainment costs Social or networking functions Fundraising or general income-growth purposes Debt servicing or financial costs Office equipment (unless an essential element in completing field work) Internships and volunteer programmes (unless benefiting an identified conservation need.)
